take: Brent holding above $100 for most of the past month despite tanker-tracking and bank reports pointing to looser balances is the key signal, with the EIA lifting Q4 Brent above $100 on Saudi pipeline attacks and tight diesel markets whilst Q3 crude prices and refinery margins rose on persistent Middle East conflict. Bunker prices have jumped roughly three-quarters since the US-Iran war began on 28 February, with Singapore VLSFO assessed at $509 per tonne, and Ship & Bunker has raised its Q4 outlook by another $124/mt — that is a direct, escalating cost into dry bulk and container voyage economics. The flow angle cuts both ways: the API flagged a 2.09 million barrel crude draw for the week ending 2 October, yet the G7's 100 million barrel IEA-coordinated release is mostly priced in, so the bullish inventory print is being offset by the known supply response. The cross-market link is the distillate complex — tight diesel is doing the heavy lifting on crude and on bunker cracks, meaning gasoil strength transmits straight into VLSFO and LSMGO, whilst the EIA's $10/bbl lift to every 2027 quarter anchors the forward curve. Watch the official EIA inventory data for confirmation of the API draw, any signs the G7 release is being absorbed faster than expected, and whether Gulf producers' new Hormuz-bypass routes translate into actual transit volumes.

items.title: What goes into diesel prices?
